newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania revolution leader says PM must resign.
newsitem.headline: Albania revolution leader says PM must resign.

text.p: A leader of Albania's 1990 democratic revolution on Friday called on Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi to resign over three get-rich-quick pyramid investment schemes that have collapsed in the country.

Azem Hajdari, who heads one of the country's leading labour unions, said the dubious schemes were a "big swindle", but he added that he did not support opposition calls for a peaceful protest against the investment schemes on Sunday.
"It is too late if Meksi resigns tomorrow, but I still call on him to resign. He should have resigned before he was elected for a second term," Hajdari told a news conference.

Meksi was nominated by President Sali Berisha of the ruling Democratic Party after a controversial general election in May and June of last year which was boycotted by most opposition parties amid claims the Democrats had manipulated the vote.

Hajdari said he regretted having to attack a fellow member and co-founder of the ruling Democratic Party who had made an "immense contribution" to the country but he said Meksi was to blame for the growth of the schemes.

The funds, which have lured thousands of Albanians into selling everything they owned with promises of big returns on small sums invested, have boomed in the Balkan nation after the fall of communism in 1990.
Three of the schemes have failed so far, and three others have suspended payments, leaving thousands of investors out of pocket in Europe's poorest country.

Hajdari hailed efforts to find a constructive solution to the crisis, but added that labour unions did not support a call by three opposition parties, including the key Socialists, for a demonstration on Tirana's main square on Sunday.
"This kind of politicising should not be supported", he said.
Hajdari welcomed the government's move on Thursday to order the seizure of some 25.5 billion leks ($255 million) deposited by the schemes in the country's commercial banks.

The government took the measure after street protests by thousands of angry depositors in one of the schemes in Tirana spread to the western port town of Vlore and the northern town of Shkoder on Thursday.
Large numbers of police remained stationed in and around Tirana on Friday to prevent a repeat of the clashes. Eyewitnesses said the situation on the streets remained calm.
Hajdari, long a thorn in the side of Berisha, was expelled from the Democratic Party three days ago but has not accepted his ousting and kept his parliamentary seat as an independent.
He said he had been elected president of a coordinative council which would unify more than a dozen trade union groups representing some 130,000 workers.
Hadjari was elected as head of the country's biggest union body, the Independent Trade Unions, last year, but a court later ruled he could not take up his post.
